final.memo:
Charlie and I have reviewed the business, but we find the investment to be outside our circle of competence due to the opaqueness of its financial-products subsidiary [D01]. While the company owns insurance franchises that may have value, the enterprise is currently marred by a $13.16 billion net loss in the first half of 2008 and a highly uncertain capital position [D01].

We cannot quantify the ultimate cash requirements arising from the company's super-senior credit-default-swap portfolio [D01]. Because these potential liabilities remain unbounded, we are unable to determine an intrinsic value, rendering any investment a gamble rather than a reasoned allocation of capital [D01], [D05].

Management has pledged to reduce the risk profile, yet the current liquidity stress and the risk of collateral calls on the interconnected guarantee book present an existential threat [D01], [D05]. Our priority is the permanent preservation of capital and Berkshire's reputation; we will not risk either on situations where we cannot calculate the downside [D01].

Though the shares trade at 0.164x book value, this discount does not offer a margin of safety when the underlying liabilities could result in a total loss of shareholders' equity [D01], [D04]. We prefer the certainty of cash in T-bills to the undefined risks inherent in this conglomerate [D01].
